model.name: Sales Lead / Opportunity
model.purpose: Represent one governed commercial pursuit from an originating lead signal through an explicitly qualified opportunity so agents can coordinate need, fit, stakeholders, activities, value, stage, probability, forecast and outcome without confusing the pursuit with party, customer, account, campaign, offering, quote, order, contract or revenue masters.
model.scope_statement: Owns pursuit identity, version, profile and status; signal, source and attribution; need, demand, problem, outcome and use-case assertions; qualification dimensions and decisions; offering-fit, scope, quantity, location, timing and dependency assertions; estimated value, budget, amount type, currency, recurrence, range and basis; score, method, version, explanation, confidence, bias and calibration; stage, gate and exception assertions; probability, forecast category, expected-close and as-of assertions; stakeholder, owner, team, influence and decision-group roles; interaction, activity and next-action references; capture, deduplication, merge, split, qualify, convert, nurture, hold, reopen, win, loss, no-decision and closure evidence; quote, order, contract and outcome references; distinct clocks, provenance, privacy, retention, validation and loss-aware projections. External party, customer, account, campaign, product, offering, activity, communication, calendar, quote, order, contract, fulfilment, forecast, financial and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Pursuit identity, version, classification, lineage, origin, attribution, need, demand, offering fit, scope, quantity, timing, location, dependencies and estimated value

Qualification, score, stage, gates, probability, forecast, stakeholders, consent and preference bindings, activities, next actions, conversion, closure, outcome, clocks, provenance, privacy, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Contact, Organization, Customer, Account, Campaign, Product, Offering, Activity, Message, Calendar, Quote, Order, Contract, Fulfilment, Invoice, Payment, Revenue, Forecast Period, Records or Consent masters

Treating a lead signal as a known person, a known party as a qualified lead, a qualified lead as a customer, or qualification, score, stage, probability, forecast and outcome as mutually proving facts

Autonomous contact, consent creation, sensitive-attribute inference, adverse action, pricing, quote issuance, order acceptance, contract execution, forecast commitment, financial recognition, disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified registry supplies only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger has no settled edge. Customer and account relationships remain external; a pursuit binds them when known.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Lead signal, party, contact, customer and account
boundary_notes.distinction: Signals may be anonymous or inferred, parties and contacts have external identities, and customer or account status has its own authority. Conversion preserves lineage instead of collapsing these identities.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Campaign, offering, activity, message and calendar
boundary_notes.distinction: Attribution, fit and touchpoints are typed references; their content, execution, delivery, scheduling and master lifecycle stay external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Quote, order, contract, fulfilment, forecast and finance
boundary_notes.distinction: Estimated value and probability support a pursuit but are not price, quotation, commitment, order, contract, delivery, recognized revenue or cash. Those masters retain independent authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: TM Forum, UBL, Schema.org, privacy law, ORG, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has a distinct scope; every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-ORG-014 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen candidate relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-026 edge.
Business-to-business, consumer, public-sector, partner, marketplace, tender, subscription, regulated-sector and regional pursuits need separate profiles.
Qualification frameworks, score models, calibration, probability, forecast taxonomies, fiscal periods, quotas and revenue-recognition links require organization-specific validation.
TMF699 official path and visible release labelling are inconsistent, and every TMF, UBL, Schema.org, privacy, ORG, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI mapping needs release-pinned conformance tests.
conflicts: Lead signal, known party, qualified lead, customer or account and opportunity are related but not interchangeable.
Qualification, score, stage, probability, forecast category, expected close and actual outcome belong to separate assertion axes.
Estimated value, budget, list price, quote, order, contract, recognized revenue and cash are related but not equivalent.
Purpose, lawful basis, consent, preference and channel permission may differ and must coexist with jurisdiction and objection evidence.
regional_assumptions: Marketing contact, consent, profiling, direct marketing, record retention, tendering and contracting depend on jurisdiction, channel, sector and party type.
GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive and FTC CAN-SPAM guidance are scoped profiles, not universal law, and local implementations may add obligations.

Reject a projection that hides stage, scoring, probability, value, privacy, authority, provenance or information loss.
